lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: The résumé includes personal details that readers are not meant to weigh in hiring.
items.because: Date of birth and nationality are unrelated to qualifications and may introduce avoidable bias.

items.says: The chronology leaves a 10-month gap between the B.S. and the first listed role unexplained.
The 35% accuracy improvement lacks a starting value and does not say whether it is relative or a percentage-point gain.
items.because: Without a baseline, readers cannot determine the final quality or interpret the improvement.

items.says: The two percentage reductions are missing the word “by.”
“GRPO” and “SFT” are not defined on first use.
The latency reduction does not identify the measured statistic.
items.because: Mean, median and tail latency can give materially different impressions of performance.

items.says: The regression count gives neither the failures’ severity nor the acceptance threshold they violated.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether the regressions were marginal fluctuations or release-blocking failures.

items.says: Assistant-only loss masking does not directly train the model to reproduce separate tool-output messages.
items.because: The mask excludes tool-output tokens from the training loss, and no improved output fidelity is measured.

items.says: The adapter fine-tuning method is repeated without adding a distinct contribution.
items.because: The earlier bullet already gives the method, so repeating it dilutes the stronger measured achievements.

items.says: The strongest internship result is buried in the final clause of the final bullet.
items.because: Leading with the 68% backlog reduction would make the business impact visible immediately.

items.says: “ML-extracted features” is too broad to identify the machine-learning approach.
The backlog reduction is missing the word “by.”
“Eight weeks” is inconsistent with the entry’s use of numerals.
A 4x reduction in total GPU memory from switching to BF16 mixed precision is technically unsupported as written.
items.because: BF16 at most halves storage for converted tensors, while other memory can remain FP32; a 4x total result requires additional changes.

items.says: The memory reduction does not say what practical capability or constraint it changed.
“Fail” incorrectly shifts to present tense within an ended role.
“Maintained” and “adds” incorrectly mix past and present tense.
items.because: The role ended in July 2024, so both actions should be in the past tense.

items.says: The release-cycle result gives the final duration without the prior duration.
items.because: Without the baseline, readers cannot quantify the benefit of the automation.

items.says: The line leads with routine maintenance and buries the stronger automation contribution.
items.because: Readers scanning its first words see upkeep rather than the change that shortened release cycles.

items.says: “Automated regression checks” does not identify the model-release property they protected.
The strongest systems-migration bullet is not first in the entry.
items.because: Migrating 30 services and eliminating dispatch delays shows greater scope and consequence than the current opening bullet.

items.says: “AI-first engineering practices” is undefined jargon rather than a concrete implementation.
items.because: It conceals the workflow, tool or quality mechanism personally introduced.

items.says: The claimed delivery and downstream benefits are generic and unsupported by a specific change or result.
items.because: Readers cannot distinguish a measured improvement from a statement of positive intent.

items.says: The strongest quantified context-management result is not the opening bullet.
items.because: The stress-test figures would make the project more credible than the generic adoption statement.

items.says: The bounded-context result does not show whether useful agent performance survived compaction.
“Under” makes the tested fan-out level ambiguous.
The fan-out test gives no before-and-after failure evidence.
items.because: It does not show the previous failure frequency or zero failures across a defined test.

items.says: The metric description is too broad to show which methods were implemented or how they were integrated.
The integration bullet does not say what capability it enabled or gap it closed.
The correlation does not identify the two variables or rankings compared.
items.because: Without the paired orderings, readers cannot tell what the correlation proves about the evaluator.

items.says: The strongest validation result is not the opening bullet.
items.because: The correlation across more than 400 trials is stronger evidence than the implementation count alone.

items.says: “Injected degradation” is opaque jargon.
“Showed” describes the validation action too generically.
The bullet wrongly attributes the internship’s industrial-inspection achievement to the research-agent project.
items.because: The same 800+ signal triage work appears under the internship, with a different backlog figure and no explained adaptation.

items.says: “Pending-case backlog” is redundant.
items.because: A backlog already consists of pending work.

items.says: The backlog reduction does not state the period over which it occurred.
items.because: A reduction over days, weeks or months would imply different operational performance.

items.says: The screening description does not explain the machine-learning method or triage decision.
items.because: “Triage branch” does not identify the workflow, and “ML-extracted” does not identify how the features were produced.
